s02.slug: THURSDAY · 9:20 AM · HOLLIS HALL, 314 — HALE’S OFFICE
body: The leaf blower on the quad has been at it since eight, one man shoving the same drift of eucalyptus bark from one side of the walk to the other, and through the window of Hollis 314 the Pacific is doing its morning silver as though nothing had happened to anybody. Jack has read the card on the glass twice on his way in and is still not sure it’s a joke.

body.title: Taped under the gold leaf
body.text: Office hours Thursday, nine to ten, and not a minute over. The dog is not in. —A.H.

body: The wine stain is still shaped like Italy. The leash hangs on its hook. Under the desk Berkeley’s blanket is empty and the long dent in it has gone shallow, and Hale, in the green tie, soup and all, is packing a satchel with the speed of a man who has left better cities than this one: a blue folder, a toothbrush in its own leather sleeve, a shirt he smooths once with the flat of his hand.
“Mr. Costigan.” He doesn’t look up. “You’ve come about the plural.”
“You wrote ‘those of you who will be in Louisiana.’” Jack stops just inside the door. “I hadn’t asked yet.”
“You’ve been asking since the landing. Ask, then, and briefly. I have a taxi at ten past and a lecture to finish in the back of it.”
“How’s Berkeley?” Jack says first, because the blanket is empty and somebody ought to.

“The city is flourishing and insufferable, and I am flying to it at eleven. You mean the dog.” Hale rolls a pair of socks. “With Mr. Marsh. Mr. Marsh reads to him. Kierkegaard, aloud. The dog has never been happier and can’t hear a word.” He rolls another pair. “He has put it behind him, which is a method I commend to the rest of us.”

Jack gets the whole picture at once: Evan Marsh at the kitchen table with his glasses on, doing *Fear and Trembling* in his seminar voice to a deaf greyhound under the same kitchen table. That is as near to Wednesday as Hale means to come, and Jack, who is done with Wednesday, leaves it where Hale put it.
Hale points the toothbrush at the other chair. Jack takes the edge of it, bag on his knees, hands out of his pockets, the nuns’ habit.

“I need the week.” He worked it out on the walk over and gives it in order. “Monday the eighth. Thursday the eleventh. Monday the fifteenth is Presidents’ Day, so that one’s a gift. Thursday the eighteenth. Three seminars. It’s the Super Bowl, or the city for it. A van, thirty hours, six people, a seating chart with a legend.”
Hale hears out the arithmetic to the eighteenth. Then, as if it were a footnote he was checking: “And who invited you? Or did you invite yourself?”
“A grandmother. She called at seven this morning.”
“Then it’s closed.” He wedges the shirt down the side of the satchel. “A grandmother is the one invitation that is also a summons.”
Against Jack’s hip the RAZR goes off, and he has it half out of the pocket before he remembers the room.
“Answer it,” Hale says, “or I shall have to listen to it die.”

body: He answers with his thumb under the edge of the chair, and the day, which has been gray and careful since Wednesday night, goes a little bright. He is lighter than he has any right to be, and he knows which part of that is the sacrament and which part is a girl who texts in lowercase.
“Go.” Hale lowers the flap of the satchel over the folder. “Write me something about it.”
“About what?”
Hale lets the question stand. Out on the quad the blower cuts off, and in the quiet it has nowhere to go.
“You’ll know when you’re in it,” he says. “That’s rather the point of the place.”
“It’s a football game, mostly. The Saints.”

“Named for the communion of the blessed and played, until January, like the other lot.” Hale shakes his head. “I have never understood the game. Eleven men confer, there is a collision, and a man in a striped shirt is blamed. I have chaired worse committees and been blamed for them.”

body.text: Jack had meant to leave the next part out. “Theo says you’ll take four thousand words on the theology of the second line. Not one of them *liminal*.” It comes out of him anyway. “I told him he made it up.”

body: “Did he.” Hale puts down the toothbrush. He pushes his glasses up into his hair and studies the ceiling, and almost smiles, which Jack has seen him do perhaps twice. “That’s very good. I’ll take it. Four thousand, and not one of them liminal. For years I have waited for someone to forbid it in writing. It is the most overworked bollocks in the humanities, Mr. Costigan, and half this campus has liminal’d itself into an early grave. Tell Mr. Vance that in my experience the difference between a lie and a prophecy is one of timing.”
“Is it a grade?”
“It is an essay. I find the distinction restful.”
“I’ve already got the first sentence,” Jack says. “The band goes out slow and comes back loose.”

“That is the whole thing, and you have spent it on the first line.” Hale lifts the flap again. “Mine is longer. They take their dead to the cemetery behind a brass band playing a dirge, and on the way home the band plays something else and the whole street dances.” The Housman goes in on top of the folder. “It is the only Christian thing I have ever envied.”
He turns to the shelf.
What comes down is an old paperback, the spine gone white in creases, the pages swollen from being read in a bath, *The Moviegoer*, with pencil down every margin in a small upright hand.

“Percy was a physician. He caught consumption, lay in a sanatorium reading Kierkegaard, and was received into the Church, which I hold against him. The book I forgive.” He holds it out. “It’s set there. It ends on Ash Wednesday. Mind the margins. They’re mine and they’re younger than I am. It’s Monday’s reading anyway, so you’ll have a head start. Read it in the passenger seat, Mr. Costigan. Never in the one with the wheel.”

Jack opens it at random. Beside a paragraph about a sunset Hale has written *Quite*, and three pages on, *Quite not*. It goes into his back pocket, and the Chesterton comes out of the pocket and into his bag to make room.
“Thirty hours in a motorcar with your contemporaries,” Hale says, doing up the buckles at last. “I should like to be the luggage.”
There is a name in that which Hale hasn’t said, and Jack has no use for it.
Down on the drive a taxi gives one apologetic honk.

journal.title: Prof. Adrian Hale
journal.text: Wrote *The Consolations of Disbelief*. Wrote me a postcard. Walked into Hollis 302 at 1:07 with wine on his cuff and asked us to prove we have souls. Saw my face at the Anchor before he could put it to the nine pages. Called me a spaniel. Some nights he drinks alone in the Anchor’s back booth after midnight and says Housman to the window. Tips like he’s apologizing. Wrote his doctorate on moral luck. Asked me if the lucky one sleeps. Lent me his own copy of Williams’s *Moral Luck*, his Oxford pencil arguing with Williams in the margins on a first-name basis. Wants it back with mine in it. I owe him more than one. Gave me a pocket Housman for Danny, foxed, wartime. No margins. They’d only erase them. Has a deaf old greyhound named Bishop Berkeley. Brought him to the Blessing of the Animals to annoy Fr. Osei. Osei finished his limerick for him. Asked me if the Housman had gone. Says when you leave something, look at it. Newman did. Threw a dinner at the cliff end of Del Playa. Told a man asking Yusuf about Fort Hood that Yusuf’s a guest, not a spokesman. Read our margins out loud. Stopped in the middle of Lena’s, and folded it away. Told Caleb he doesn’t answer devotion. Collected our margins. Read Lena’s on mine: Neither do I. The final’s oral, December 16th — each of us defends the other’s best argument, and he’s the opponent. Told the room to keep Yusuf’s chair. The last seminar: Lena said nothing for an hour, and he told us to note the date. By Friday we each email him which of the other’s arguments we’ll defend. If we pick a weak one, he’ll know. Both picks came in. Not surprised, not disappointed — at his age the same thing as joy. Wednesday, two o’clock. Come as you are. The oral: she’d sent him Augustine. Lena first, then me. He knew which one I’d picked. I don’t yet know what I know, he said. He said it was an argument; he’s told they still occur. Marks posted on the solstice. I did well, which he’d like me to understand is not the same as being right. He and Berkeley are spending Christmas in Marisol. Spring: PHIL 109H, The Novel as Moral Argument, Mondays and Thursdays at one in Hollis 302. Opposite ends of the table, for the safety of the others. He got the baby in the king cake. ‘For the first quarter of an hour you were civil, and I didn’t care for it. I find I care for this even less.’ Carthage is not on the syllabus. The Conversion of St. Paul: he did Saul for Caleb. He’s in New York Thursday, being rude to a churchman on a stage, so Greene moved to his house Wednesday with the State of the Union on — phones in the dog’s bowl, bring a guest, sides assigned: me for Sarah’s silence, Lena against. Opposite ends of a door. He turned the President off before the rebuttal. When Lena and I went at each other across his table he stood up and stopped it, in a voice I’ve never heard out of him, and he wasn’t amused. Berkeley felt it through the floor. On the deck he said the table was his. He asked where a Catholic goes at eight on a Wednesday. Give him my regards. He blessed my dog. He may like to do it again. Monday he gave us Joyce, “The Dead,” and taught it as if Wednesday never happened, and everybody at the table knew what it was for. He kept Lena after with the door shut. Then me: until Wednesday no argument at his table had ever sent the dog under the kitchen table. He said I went for the places that hurt, that I’m good at it, and that he’d rather I weren’t. Miss Ivors left before the goose. Nobody remembers what she was right about. Thursday he canceled the seminar for a lecture in Berkeley and gave me the week. Go. Write me something about it. Four thousand words on the second line, not one of them *liminal* — Theo’s terms; he took them. He lent me his own *Moviegoer*, his pencil in the margins. It ends on Ash Wednesday. Thirty hours in a van: he’d like to be the luggage.

choices.key: Hale gave you the week: go, write him something about it. You told him you’re going for the Saints.
response: “It’s the Saints. Ask anyone in the van.”

“I’m sure you would.” Hale is already onto Percy: his hero goes to the pictures to be certified, and a place isn’t real to him until he’s seen it on a screen. “A football game does the same work with more beer.” He gets the strap over his shoulder and holds the door with his free hand, and Jack goes out under his arm into the corridor with the whole of New Orleans in his back pocket.

choices.text: “I’ll write you four thousand on whether a Browns fan can be saved.”
choices.key: Hale gave you the week: go, write him something about it. You offered him four thousand words on whether a Browns fan can be saved. Three, he said, as an appendix.
response: “Three,” Hale says. “As an appendix to the four. Theology has limits, and the Browns are the limit.”

“Put the Browns last. They’ll be glad of the company.” He winds the strap once round his fist and holds the door with the other hand, and Jack goes down a corridor that smells of floor wax and somebody’s toast with an appendix to plan.

choices.key: Hale gave you the week: go, write him something about it. You said you’d write it.
response: “I know,” Hale says. “That’s why I said yes.”

He holds the satchel out to Jack by its strap. “Carry this down for me.” In five months Jack has been handed essays, rebukes and a Housman, and never once somebody’s luggage. He takes it, and it weighs more than a satchel ought. Hale comes after him down the stairs with his coat over his arm, slower than he has moved all morning, and neither of them mentions the stairs.

choices.text: “Are you going to tell me to be careful?”
choices.key: Hale gave you the week: go, write him something about it. You asked if he was going to tell you to be careful. He told you to take notes.
response: “No,” Hale says. “I’m going to tell you to take notes.”

He sets the satchel on the carpet with the strap trailing and answers it properly. “Careful is what people say when they’ve given up on interesting.” He bends for the strap, finds the door with his heel, and holds it open on the corridor, where the blower has started up again.
